Ionization potential or energy: Electron of an atom can be removed by supplying energy. This energy is known as ionization energy or ionization potential or ionization enthalpy. Thus it is defined as "the minimum energy* ',.vhich is required to remove the most loosely bounded electron (valence electron) from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state". It is denoted by I.E. or I.P. and expressed in electron volt (eV). lev per atom = 96.3 kJ/mole Na + I.E. -...-.-.-.-..-.......+ + e— Mg + I.E. -...........-...........-...-.> Mg2+ + 2e— Atomic Size: I.E. decrease with increase in atomic size because the larger the distance from the nucleus, the lesser will be the attraction between the nucleus and the valence electrons.

Nuclear Charge: The greater the number of protons, the greater the attraction of the electrons to the nucleus and the harder it is to remove the electrons. The number of protons in the nucleus is known as the nuclear charge. So, the greater the value of nuclear charge, more difficult will it be to remove an electron.
